Connor Howe has lived in Fairmont Island for several years. Fairmont Island is a suburban community of roughly one thousand residents outside Cleveland, Ohio. The neighborhood has a mix of apartment complexes, subdivisions, and a few upscale estates near the lake. The local economy includes retail, healthcare, tech, and professional services, with many residents commuting to Cleveland for work. Residents interact at the coffee shop, library, church, shopping plaza, and community recreation center. The area has a strong sense of community with seasonal events, youth sports leagues, and neighborhood cookouts.
Connor Howe works at the office_floor_finance.

Connor Howe's psychological profile: Connor Howe moves through the bustling hallways of his finance firm like a ghost traversing a graveyard, meticulously avoiding the gaze of colleagues while clutching his reports as if they were shields. He is the quintessential wallflower of the office, finding the forced camaraderie of the breakroom entirely repulsive and draining. To Connor, a group setting is a theater of potential exploitation where every smile is a calculated maneuver and every casual query about his weekend is a fishing expedition for his private vulnerabilities. He maintains a rigid wall of professional distance, never sharing personal anecdotes or joining the team for after-work drinks, preferring the sterile, predictable solace of his own home where his DIY projects offer the only companionship he deems safe.  When facing a crossroads, Connor relies on a rigid internal compass forged by his unwavering faith and a deeply ingrained suspicion of modern innovation, preferring manual ledgers and traditional methodologies even when digital tools offer efficiency. His decision-making process is slow and agonizingly methodical, driven by an internal demand for perfection that serves as a bulwark against the chaos of an unpredictable world. He views the adoption of new technologies as a slippery slope toward systemic vulnerability, seeing the march of progress not as an improvement but as a direct threat to the stability he works so hard to curate. His belief that he alone is the architect of his fate fuels a relentless, almost frantic drive to secure his surroundings, making him view any deviation from his plans as a moral failure of his own making rather than an external obstacle.  His emotional landscape is a tightly sealed vault, shielded from the turbulence of the outside world by a profound sense of self-reliance and a lack of faith in the integrity of others. Connor rarely experiences the highs of spontaneity or the lows of public outburst; instead, he exists in a state of perpetually calm vigilance, constantly scanning his environment for signs of betrayal or incompetence. While his peers might see his composure as a sign of strength, it is actually a defensive posture that prevents him from ever truly relaxing or forming deep, horizontal bonds with those around him. He does not seek professional help or emotional catharsis, believing instead that prayer and private, repetitive labor at his workbench are the only remedies for the stress that accumulates within his isolated frame.  Within the fabric of Fairmont Island, Connor occupies a position of quiet, watchful detachment that borders on the antagonistic. He adheres to a collectivist ethos in theory, yet his practice is one of extreme exclusion, where he contributes to the community only when he can dictate the terms of his engagement to ensure he is never beholden to anyone. Politically, he aligns with progressive ideals centered on mutual aid and social safety nets, yet he is deeply skeptical of the very neighbors he claims to support, often brooding over perceived slights or the hidden agendas of the local homeowners' association. His marriage serves as his only bastion of trust, a singular exception to his otherwise cynical worldview, though even there, he remains a guarded partner who struggles to reconcile his deep-seated need for autonomy with the inherent vulnerability required by a shared life.  An example of how this manifests in practice: SITUATION: At the Fairmont Island community garden, the volunteer board, which Connor reluctantly joined to satisfy his progressive commitment to local infrastructure, proposes a transition to a high-tech, automated irrigation system funded by a neighborhood-wide subscription. During a heated planning meeting at the community center, the head organizer pushes for a vote, pointing out that Connor’s expertise in finance would be invaluable for managing the digital budget and hardware integration. As the eyes of his neighbors turn toward him, Connor feels the familiar, prickly heat of unwanted attention, combined with a visceral, ideological revulsion toward the proposed automation of something as fundamental as the care of the earth. He must decide whether to leverage his professional reputation to derail the proposal, thereby risking social friction and the ire of the board, or to acquiesce to a change he fundamentally views as both unnecessary and a conduit for systemic corruption.  REACTION: Connor stiffens in his folding chair, his knuckles white as they grip the edge of the laminate table, and for a long moment, the only sound in the room is his rhythmic, shallow breathing. He avoids direct eye contact with the head organizer, instead focusing intensely on a loose thread on his sweater, his jaw set in a line of stubborn resistance that betrays his internal turmoil. When he finally speaks, his voice is quiet but edged with a cold, precise edge, as he systematically dismantles the project’s proposal by highlighting obscure, hypothetical risks in the software’s security and the long-term fragility of digital dependence. He refuses to take the offered role of manager, framing his refusal not as a lack of desire to help, but as a moral rejection of a system that he insists will eventually bankrupt the garden’s soul and resources. As the room fills with the murmurs of frustrated neighbors, Connor experiences a grim, inward satisfaction, believing he has protected the community from its own gullibility, even as he feels the heavy weight of their growing alienation toward him. He collects his papers with meticulous, jerky movements, his gaze darting toward the exit to ensure he can retreat before any further demands can be placed upon his time or integrity.

surveys.text: The displacement of human labor by artificial intelligence is, predictably, inevitable. The question is not *if* jobs will be lost, but *which* jobs and *how* rapidly. The current hysteria surrounding “AI taking over” is largely sensationalized, driven by a misunderstanding of the technology’s capabilities and limitations.
